_doc: MANABIT autonomous loop backlog. Protocol: design/process/autonomous-loop.md. The loop PICKS the highest `priority` item whose `gate` is `loop`. Items gated `owner` are never picked - they are mirrored into loop/owner-queue.md and wait. Rescore after every iteration. Items with gate `closed` are kept as a record of a reconciliation miss, not as available work - see `_reconciliation`.

_scoring.lift: 1-5, expected enjoyment gain. 5 = moves 3+ personas or repairs a headline promise.
_scoring.evidence: 0-3. 3 = a number from a committed artifact (tools/sim/out/*, a seeded probe). 2 = observed directly (rendered frame, live probe) but not root-caused. 1 = reasoned from the design. 0 = taste alone.
_scoring.risk: 1-5 blast radius. 5 = frozen section 13 contract, save schema, or a final taste call -> AUTO-ESCALATE, never picked.
_scoring.law: An item with evidence < 2 may not be built. It may only be MEASURED - build the instrument first, then rescore. This is the rule that stopped wave 1 shipping two wrong-way changes on vibes.

items.title: New-player legibility: fragility + overweight nudge, and an honest 'defanged' loss reason
items.why: R3 / D3. outcome() returns SURVIVABLE_LOSS the moment has_offensive_move() is false (combat.gd:172), but is_deployable() needs only ONE offensive bit. A deploy-legal core+1-arm build passes the Workshop gate then loses on turn 1 before the player acts. Novice own-build ventures lose 58.3% of the pos0 Rusty skirmish. The loss screen says nothing about why.
items.criterion: PRE-STATE before building: a one-offensive-bit build shows a build-time fragility warning in the BalanceMeter, and the defang loss path prints a distinct reason string. Verified in a rendered frame (L3) plus a smoke_layout/smoke_builder assertion. No change to combat.gd resolution.

items.title: Junction lane labels tell the truth about risk
items.why: R7 / D8. Measured per-mod outcomes: overgrown ('the foe fields heavier bits') is the SAFEST lane at DEATH 0.00, tailwind ('mended 4 HP', sounds like a gift) is the DEADLIEST at DEATH 0.59. The menace label is the safe pick. This directly violates the project's own standing law that card text IS the rule and the FTL lying-label anti-pattern is banned.
items.persona: QA Hunter + Optimizer (decision depth: a choice you cannot read is not a choice)
items.criterion: PRE-STATE: per-lane DEATH rate ordering matches the ordering a player would infer from the printed card text, measured on the existing sessions aggregate. Elite fork only - the BOSS fork rusted lane is already correctly the harder pick and must stay.

items.title: Restore elite core-hunt stakes (Pindrop structural, Sable undertuned)
items.why: R1 / D1. Two of six 'core-hunting' elites have a 0% DEATH rate. Pindrop is STRUCTURAL: its loadout is HEAD MULTI / ARM_L GUARD / ARM_R MULTI / BACK MULTI, zero SINGLE moves, and the core-hunt branch (combat.gd:146-152) only fires for archetype==SINGLE, so it can never land a killing blow (0/60). Sable has 2 SINGLE moves but is too weak (0/60). Cogsworth 30/60, Brassmore 49/60 confirm the probe is sound. The panel calls this the single highest-leverage change.
items.persona: QA Hunter + Cozy Collector + the difficulty curve (3 lenses at once)
items.criterion: PRE-STATE: Pindrop and Sable each reach a DEATH rate inside the elite band set by Cogsworth (30/60) and Thornlash (24/60) - NOT above Brassmore. Re-measure with tools/sim/qa_verify.gd. CH-05/CH-06 were reverted once on wrong-way criteria; re-apply only with the band stated first and revert again if it moves wrong.

items.title: The modal first Box of Scrap should not be a guaranteed death
items.why: R3 / D2. Kit survival by grade is a step function: Dud/Rough/Fair all ~0.00 at every skill tier, Keen 0.86-1.00, Gleaming 1.00. Fair is the 32% modal roll, so P(survive first box) ~= 0.25 and the median FIRST free kit dies 100% at the boss regardless of play. Real stakes are intended; a guaranteed-loss modal first experience is a new-player cliff.
items.criterion: PRE-STATE: P(survive) for a player's first N boxes rises above a stated floor without flattening the Gleaming payoff. Options: a first-boxes pity floor, or a clearer grade-power read at crack time so a Fair box reads as a short outing rather than a run. Re-measure on smoke_kit_sim per-lane bands.

items.title: Boss difficulty should rise, not fall (Gildfall folds, Brassmore is the wall)
items.why: R4 / D4. Under optimal aggression the ch8 FINALE Prince Gildfall is WIN 1.000 / DEATH 0.000 while the EARLIER ch4 Sunking Brassmore is WIN 0.305 / DEATH 0.695. The finale folds to the exact tech a player has already found by the earlier boss. The identical ~0.12 ladder win rates are a greedy-AI artifact hiding this.
items.criterion: PRE-STATE: measured WIN under the RACE policy is monotonically non-increasing across ch4 -> ch8. Fix by giving Gildfall real core defense (guard/mend when threatened) or by swapping boss order.
items.touches: Challenger loadouts / AI behaviour. Frozen surfaces: combat.gd resolution OFF LIMITS.
items.closed_evidence: Gildfall given grandpeal; RACE WIN 1.000 -> 0.305, GUARD DEATH 0.775 vs Brassmore 0.550; Brassmore unmoved

items.title: Rarity should not be an inverted value signal
items.why: R6 / D10. Mean win-rate deltas: EPIC arm_seer -0.0058 and EPIC pocketful_arm_grinlet -0.1225 are NEGATIVE, while COMMON grumble_co_girder_fist +0.191 and COMMON errant_core_pledge +0.165 are among the strongest. Grinlet at -0.1225 is a genuine dead bit. Players see rarity and raw stats and no counter-data. Rarity is not uniformly wrong (EPIC bedrock legs +0.34) - it is unreliable, which is worse than a known-flat signal.
items.persona: Optimizer + Cozy Collector (a chase item that makes you weaker poisons collection)
items.criterion: PRE-STATE: both negative EPICs land above a stated delta floor after repricing, measured on the roster sim, without pushing any bit past the existing band ceiling.
items.touches: parts/catalog_extra.json stats. Frozen surfaces: the 13 base fixtures are hardcoded and OFF LIMITS.
items.closed_by: CH-P9 (+ a producer ruling on seer)
items.closed_evidence: pocketful_arm_grinlet now SINGLE power 8, mean_delta -0.1225 -> +0.1242. arm_seer is a BASE FIXTURE and frozen; ruled statistically neutral, no-change

items.title: Coffer odds string reads as a typo: 'C70 R22 E8 %'
items.why: Observed in a rendered frame (loop/out/shots/shot_coffer_nook.png, shot_barrow.png). The trailing bare '%' after the last number reads like a stray glyph rather than a unit applying to all three. Odds legibility is the honest-information promise of the Coffer Nook and it is the first number a new player is asked to trust.
items.criterion: PRE-STATE: the odds line reads unambiguously as three percentages in a rendered frame, at the same or smaller width (the 720px layout budget has zero slack - smoke_layout must stay green).
items.touches: ui coffer/broker copy. Frozen surfaces: none.
items.closed_evidence: Odds now derived from PackRoller thresholds via odds_line(); both call sites (broker_screen.gd:202-203, chest_screen.gd:307) ask the roller. Reads "5 bits - C70% R22% E8% - rare+ guaranteed". New smoke_broker assertions, proven red on label-math drift.

items.title: Audit the saturated cyan panel on the Brass Coffer lid against the warm palette
items.why: Observed in shot_coffer_nook.png: a bright saturated cyan rectangle sits on the coffer lid inside an otherwise warm brass/wood frame. It may be the intended Glimmer/mana tell, but at that saturation it reads as an untextured placeholder rather than etched-rune plastic with a soft mana glow. Needs a root-cause read against the art bible before it is called a defect.
items.criterion: MEASURE FIRST: identify the source material/token, compare against the DESIGN.md palette tokens, and either confirm it as intended (close the item) or reprice the colour. Do not repaint on taste alone.
items.touches: coffer face render / Tokens. Frozen surfaces: none.
items.closed_evidence: Measured #7be1ff h194 v1.00 against DESIGN.md: matched no token and exceeded every token value. Remapped 779 pixels onto --affinity-mana #3FA890 with shading preserved. smoke_art gained a coffer-face palette check, proven red on the original asset.

items.title: Proving Grounds spoils lines name bits but never their value
items.why: R7 tail, corroborated in shot_proving.png: every challenger row lists 'Spoils: <bit names>' with no worth attached, while the wager loop asks the player to weigh a scrap stake against those spoils. The panel separately measured the loot gradient INVERTED (stake-10 Cogsworth loots a melt-45 EPIC; stake-20 Gildfall loots melt-20), so the reward does not track the difficulty and the screen gives the player nothing to notice that with.
items.persona: Optimizer + Newcomer (an informed wager needs both numbers)
items.criterion: PRE-STATE: a rendered frame shows spoils value alongside the stake on every challenger row, within the row height budget, smoke_layout green. Whether to also FIX the inverted gradient is a separate balance item.
items.closed_evidence: ui/proving_screen.gd appends "(melts for scrap N-M)" derived from Broker.salvage_scrap. smoke_bout asserts the advertised worth equals what PlayerState.melt_bit actually pays - two independent paths - proven red by making the payout drift. The "inverted loot gradient" half was REFUTED by measurement (tools/sim/wager_probe.gd): floor and ceiling both rise with stake.

items.title: INSTRUMENT: a decision-density probe for the build screen
items.why: The Optimizer scores 5/10 because 'the legal build collapses to one greedy answer identical across every core' and 'the soul pick is nearly cosmetic'. That is currently a reasoned claim, not a measured one - there is no instrument that counts how many distinct builds are within X% of optimal under the weight cap. Every other headline claim in the loop is numbers-grounded; this one is not, so under the evidence law it cannot be built against yet.
items.criterion: Build the probe FIRST: report the count of distinct near-optimal builds per core and the overlap between them. Then rescore L-10 into a real balance item with evidence 3.

items.title: Turn cap / wall-fight pacing (D13 ADR)
items.why: R2 / D7. combat.gd outcome() has no turn counter. 27.2% of damaging hits land for exactly 1 (the DEF floor at combat.gd:107). Cogsworth-mirror resolves at turn 167; GUARD-vs-Brassmore at 221. The ladder top is uncappable (reached_top 0.00 at every tier). Fights provably terminate, so this is a grind not a lock - but it is a 5-10 minute slog and it caps the ladder.
items.blocked_by: The resolver is section 13 frozen. A turn cap needs a tiebreak rule (core-HP %) and that is an owner ADR, not a loop edit.
items.corroborated: Change order section C: D7 deferred, needs the section-13 turn-cap ADR (D13).

items.title: Cozy endgame bundle: coffer RNG persistence, a Glimmer sink, a discovery faucet
items.why: R5 / D5+D6+D9. PlayerState._init always runs PackRoller.new(20260711) and SaveManager persists no roller or pity field, so every fresh boot replays a byte-identical brass stream and every new player cracks the identical 'surprises' - coffers are relaunch-scummable. Glimmer: 57.2 earned per player over 30 days, 0.0 spent on all 30. Compendium: only 12.6% reach 80% in a month. The panel estimates this moves the Cozy Collector from 6 to ~8.
items.blocked_by: Needs save schema v5. The workbench already lists D7/D9 as owner-gated save-v5 items.
items.corroborated: Change order section C: D5 needs save v5 (schema FROZEN); D6 a new shop feature, out of bounded scope; D9 an economy/discovery-faucet pass.

items.title: Speed axis payoff (D11 ADR)
items.why: Measured dead: speed buys initiative and nothing else, the sniper attack rates sit at 0.00/0.00/0.03/0.00, and the whole silksteel core-sniper family beats nobody in the pentagon. An entire advertised build direction is inert.
items.blocked_by: Any real payoff changes resolution order or adds a resolver hook - section 13 territory. Already queued as an owner ADR in the workbench.
items.corroborated: Change order section C: D11 resolver weight-check is FROZEN. The speed-axis ADR remains separately queued in workbench.md.

items.title: Brass coffer prints EPIC 8% but actually rolls 14.8%
items.why: Measured this iteration with tools/sim/odds_probe.gd over 40,000 brass coffers (200,000 bits): realized C 63.3% / R 21.9% / E 14.8% against a printed C70 / R22 / E8. The epic-pity at 9 nearly DOUBLES the real EPIC rate. Tin is honest (85.1/11.9/3.0 vs printed 85/12/3) because it has no guarantee and no pity. The error is generous to the player, so it is not predatory - but it is still a label that does not match the roll, and the project's own law is that printed odds match the threshold verbatim (smoke_run.gd:174). It also means the pity, a real kindness, is completely invisible.
items.persona: Cozy Collector (surprise you cannot see the shape of) + QA Hunter (P3, labels never lie)
items.criterion: PRE-STATE: the printed brass line and the realized 40k-coffer distribution agree within the same +/-2pp band the tin assertion already uses, OR the line discloses the pity rule in words so the gap is explained rather than hidden. Then extend the smoke_broker empirical assertion to cover brass (it is deliberately excluded today).
items.entangled_with: D5 / L-12. The pity counter is NOT persisted (PlayerState._init always re-seeds, SaveManager stores no pity field), so realized EPIC depends on session length: 14.8% is a marathon-session upper bound and a relaunch-often player sees closer to the printed 8%. Printing a single honest number may not be possible until pity persists, which is owner-gated. Disclosing the rule in words is available now and needs no schema change.
items.touches: economy/pack_roller.gd odds_line copy, tests/smoke_broker.gd. Frozen surfaces: none.
items.closed_evidence: PackRoller.BRASS_PITY named, _roll uses it, pity_line() derives the copy. Coffer Nook and Barrow both print "never more than 9 bits without an Epic"; tin prints nothing. smoke_broker asserts the words track the constant, proven red by tampering. The 8%% vs 14.8%% gap is NOT closed - that needs one honest number, which needs persisted pity, which needs save v5 (owner Q2).

items.title: INSTRUMENT: per-screen frame verdicts, with animated screens marked UNVERIFIABLE
items.why: Iteration 6 REFUTED the cheap version by measurement. Whole-frame difference cannot separate animation phase from a real edit: animation-only drift on the Workshop is 0.291%% and a ONE-CHARACTER label change is 0.376%%, and raising the amplitude cutoff keeps the ratio flat at ~1.3x (12/40/80/120 all measured). Any threshold that ignores the breathing bob also ignores a changed label. The good news: compendium, menagerie and proving measure 0.000%% between runs, so comparison is exact on every screen WITHOUT wall-clock animation.
items.persona: n/a - this is the loop's own instrument, and it is load-bearing
items.criterion: PRE-STATE next time: the comparator returns a PER-SCREEN verdict - SAME, DIFFERENT, or UNVERIFIABLE - and reports the three animated screens (chest_screen.gd:341, workshop.gd:650, manabit_stage.gd:194) as UNVERIFIABLE rather than guessing. Prove it flags a one-character change as DIFFERENT on a static screen, and never reports SAME for an animated one. A tool that admits what it cannot see beats one that guesses.
items.closed_evidence: tools/loop/framecheck.sh returns per-screen SAME / DIFFERENT / UNVERIFIABLE. The unstable set is derived by rendering three times and taking the worst pairing as the noise floor - the Barrow drifts intermittently and is not one of the known wall-clock seams. A screen with non-zero noise is never reported SAME. Three controls run: no-change gives zero DIFFERENT; one char on zero-noise Proving gives DIFFERENT at 2.023%; the same on the noisy Workshop gives UNVERIFIABLE.

items.title: A loop run that pushes nothing must be loud, not 'succeeded'
items.why: Incident 1: two unattended runs exited SUCCEEDED having pushed nothing ($3.06, 19 min and 73 sec). The scheduler's own status field cannot distinguish 'did the work' from 'exited cleanly', so nothing in the system noticed. The only reason it was caught is that a human-driven session happened to fetch the branch.
items.criterion: PRE-STATE: a script or gate that compares the branch head before and after an iteration and fails loudly when an iteration ends with no new commit and no BLOCKED entry in loop/ledger.md. The check must be shown to fire on a deliberately empty run.
items.closed_evidence: tools/loop/verdict.sh - start records the head, check refuses an iteration with neither a commit nor a blocked report. Four negative controls run and seen to fail. Wired into Phase 0 and Phase 7 of the protocol and the skill.

items.title: The stake-10 tier is a lottery: spoils range 8-45 for a fixed price
items.why: Measured this iteration with tools/sim/wager_probe.gd. Stake 5 pays 8-8, 8-20, 8-8. Stake 10 pays 8-45, 8-45, 8-20, 8-20. Stake 20 pays 45-45 and 20-45. The gradient is monotonic (so the panel's 'inverted' claim is refuted), but at stake 10 the same price buys anything from a common to an EPIC. Two of the four stake-10 elites cap at 20 while the other two reach 45.
items.persona: Optimizer (P5 - reward tracking difficulty is about variance as well as mean)
items.criterion: MEASURE-THEN-DECIDE. This may be intended texture rather than a defect, so do NOT tune it on instinct. First state what the wager is supposed to feel like at each tier, then decide whether 8-45 at a fixed stake serves that. If it does, close this as intended and say so.
items.closed_evidence: The player CHOOSES the looted bit - ui/combat_screen.gd:1626-1638 builds one button per non-core bit under "Loot a part:". The 8-45 range is a menu, not a draw, so it is not a lottery. By what is actually taken: stake 5 -> 8/20/8, stake 10 -> 45/45/20/20, stake 20 -> 45/45. Monotonic. The real finding (flat reward ceiling from stake 10 to 20) is escalated as Q7.

items.title: The coffer lid gem is a hard-edged rectangle
items.why: Noticed while fixing L-08's colour, and deliberately not widened into that change. The seal on the brass coffer lid is a flat 34x28 rectangle with hard edges. The palette is now correct but the SHAPE still reads as a pasted-on sticker rather than an inset, faceted seal. Cozy-craft is etched-rune plastic; a rectangle with no bevel or inset shadow is neither etched nor faceted.
items.criterion: PRE-STATE: the seal reads as inset or faceted in a rendered frame - a bevel, an inset shadow, or a non-rectangular silhouette. Judge it in the frame, not in the file. If the honest answer is that it needs real art rather than a procedural tweak, say so and escalate instead of approximating.
items.closed_evidence: Filed claim REFUTED - the silhouette was already tapered (28 rows, 13 distinct widths). The real defect was measured: gem median 0.659 equalled both its own max and the brass median 0.655, so it was flat AND had no luminance separation. Regraded to median 0.502 against brass 0.655, hue held at 168 degrees, facet detail preserved as modulation. Reads as recessed in the frame; smoke_art palette gate green.

items.title: The loop's own scripts continue past a failed step
items.why: Iteration 9 shipped commit 81f33c0 with the tool but WITHOUT its ledger entry or backlog closure. The Python block that writes them died on a SyntaxError; the surrounding shell had no `set -e`, so the commit and push ran anyway. Code and record went out of sync, were pushed, and CI passed. verdict.sh passed it correctly - it proves a commit exists, never that the bookkeeping is right. Fourth silent-failure shape this session and the first to reach the remote.
items.criterion: PRE-STATE: a record step that fails must stop the iteration before the commit. Prove it by deliberately breaking the record step and showing no commit is created. Consider whether verdict.sh should also assert the ledger's newest entry has no 'pending' placeholder left in it.
items.closed_evidence: verdict.sh check now also fails on an unfilled Result placeholder and on delivered commits that never touched loop/ledger.md; BLOCKED runs stay exempt. Four controls run, including one proving no false positive from prose that merely mentions the placeholder.

_reconciliation.what: The first version of this backlog scored L-01 through L-06 as live work. All seven underlying defects had already been fixed and measured by design/balance/playtest-fixes-change-order.md (ratified 2026-07-21), which this session read the PROBLEM statement for (the playtest panel) without reading the RESPONSE to it.
_reconciliation.how_found: Flagged by a peer session, then verified in code here (challengers.gd:44,50; workshop.gd:917,921; combat_screen.gd:1042; catalog_extra.json grinlet) rather than taken on the doc's or the peer's word.
_reconciliation.cost_if_unfixed: The first two unattended iterations would have re-implemented shipped work, and the loop would have reported progress for it.
_reconciliation.protocol_fix: Phase 0 of design/process/autonomous-loop.md now requires RECONCILE: no item is picked until its defect is re-verified as still live in code. Evidence expires.
